claims.statement: The observed rear main route has 5.56 mm physical focal length, 24 mm equivalent focal length, and a verified 4080x3072 output record.

The stock camera produced an ultrawide 0.6x route with 1.64 mm physical focal length, 15 mm equivalent focal length, and 3264x2448 output, but the ordinary-app endpoint and active-sensor mechanism are unresolved.

The stock camera produced a telephoto 2x route with 7.1 mm physical focal length, 50 mm equivalent focal length, and 4096x3072 output, but the ordinary-app endpoint and active-sensor mechanism are unresolved.
Ordinary-app Camera2 enumeration exposes rear ID 0 and front ID 1 on the observed build.
Candidate IDs 2 through 5 are not openable by the ordinary diagnostic application and remain system, privileged, vendor, or otherwise filtered candidates.
The full high-resolution, reprocessing, video, constrained-high-speed, and mandatory stream-combination matrix is not yet verified.
The stock Expert interface produced distinct observed 0.6x, 1x, and 2x output records, while their internal controller-to-camera route remains bounded at an opaque stock or system transition.
External widget focal launches are stock-camera handoffs and the committed audit remained on the 5.56 mm or 24 mm-equivalent route; this does not prove direct auxiliary access.
Complete stock camera package, split, signature, install-path, runtime package, and decompilation provenance is not yet present in the repository.
The canonical observed build fingerprint is Nothing/GalagaEEA/Galaga Android 16 build 2606151653 with release keys.
Build-matched framework camera artifacts, vendor camera libraries, and firmware partitions are missing, so provider, HAL, native, configuration, permission, and SELinux interfaces remain incomplete.
The diagnostics application enumerates vendor characteristic, request, result, session, physical-request, and default-template entries while leaving unavailable Java types unknown.
No MediaTek or Nothing vendor key is production-enabled; exact-build allowlisting and a verified effective probe are mandatory before use.
The verified ordinary-app rear route is public camera ID 0 mapped to the main optical route.
Stock ultrawide and telephoto routes are bounded at unresolved stock, system, vendor, logical, or sensor-scenario transitions and are unavailable to production replacement routing.
Public zoom or crop on ID 0 must be labelled digital unless active-sensor evidence independently proves an optical or in-sensor transition.

The replacement application requests camera permission only, disables backup and cleartext traffic, and rejects network permissions, imports, and common HTTP dependencies through repository validation.
Diagnostic exports are opt-in and exclude image pixels, thumbnails, paths, content URIs, location, serials, user text, and arbitrary metadata values by default.
Portable contracts exist for burst metadata, clock calibration, scoring, reference selection, local alignment, rendering stage order, color transitions, artefact detection, and conservative fallback.
Algorithm selection, image quality, motion behavior, resource targets, and stock-versus-replacement performance are not yet verified on the physical device.

The repository contains validated portable contracts for backend lifecycle, route truthfulness, session/request planning, modes, UI state, storage, vendor isolation, privacy, diagnostics, and resource policy.

The current application can use the verified public main route, while auxiliary routing, full processing integration, measured budgets, and complete transactional recovery remain bounded by their active issues.

decisions.decision: Use public rear ID 0 as the production baseline camera endpoint.
Do not represent main-camera digital crop as ultrawide or telephoto optical output.
Keep every vendor feature disabled until an exact-build probe verifies effective behavior and a public fallback exists.
Keep all image processing on-device and deny network capability in the production application.
Use private-by-default metadata and omit optional sensitive fields when consent is absent.
Use bounded request retry, session recreation, and camera reopen policies; never loop permanent failures.
Prefer the selected reference frame or reduced processing over forced multi-frame artefacts.
Treat every untested firmware build as incompatible with existing vendor and auxiliary allowlists until diagnostics are rerun.
Reference private diagnostics and user images by metadata and hashes without redistributing raw artifacts.

updateTriggers: A new Nothing OS build fingerprint is tested.
The stock camera package version, splits, signature, or install path changes.
A vendor or auxiliary route changes from unknown to verified or from verified to rejected.
New provider, HAL, framework, policy, or native artifacts are acquired.
Device benchmarks replace hypothetical processing or resource targets.
A material claim changes confidence, evidence, build scope, or implementation use.
